title: Analysis of chlorophyll and carotenoid compounds in eucalyptus leaves
author: Nicolas Younes
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.pex-2395/v1
materials: Extract absorbance values (A) for the following wavelengths:
664 nm (to allow for calculation of carotenoids).

steps.title: Punch leaf discs
steps.instruction: Using a hole‑punch, remove five discs from each eucalyptus leaf sample, avoiding mid‑veins and any damaged areas (see Figure 1).

steps.title: Weigh discs and place in tube
steps.instruction: Weigh the punched discs on a precision balance, record the weight, and transfer the discs into a labeled micro‑centrifuge tube.

steps.title: Add ethanol extraction solvent
steps.instruction: Add exactly 2 mL of ethanol to each tube containing the leaf discs.

steps.title: Vortex and incubate overnight
steps.instruction: Vortex each tube for 30 seconds, then place the tubes in a refrigerator set to 4 °C and let them extract for 24 hours.

steps.title: Vortex homogenisation next day
steps.instruction: After the 24‑hour incubation, vortex each tube briefly to re‑homogenise the extract.

steps.title: Centrifuge extracts
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes for 5 minutes at 3500 rpm in an explosion‑proof tabletop centrifuge maintained at 4 °C.

steps.title: Aliquot extract to microplate
steps.instruction: Transfer 200 µL of the supernatant from each sample into wells of a 96‑well microplate; include an ethanol blank in the first well and repeat a blank every 15–20 samples.

steps.title: Measure absorbance spectra
steps.instruction: Using a spectrophotometer, record absorbance of each well against the ethanol blank over the full wavelength range 350 nm to 1000 nm.

steps.title: Calculate pigment concentrations
steps.instruction:
Apply the measured absorbance values (A664, A649, A470) to the following equations to obtain pigment concentrations (µg mL⁻¹):
(1) Ca = 13.36·A664 – 5.19·A649
(2) Cb = (27/43)·A649 – 8.12·A664
(3) Cx+c = [1000·A470 – 2.13·Ca – (97/63)·Cb] / 209
(References: Sumanta et al., 2014; Ritchie, 2006).
